text:
Dallas outchanced St. Louis by 0.73 expected goals and walked off with a 4-0 loss, because Joel Hofer stopped all 25 shots he faced. The numbers had him saving 2.89 goals more than those shots deserved, and Dallas had a 59 percent chance of winning if this game were replayed. The best look Dallas missed was a 29 percent chance for Mikko Rantanen in the second period, and it went off target.

STL did its scoring in bursts. Mason McTavish opened the night 1:34 into the first with a snap shot off feeds from Colton Parayko and Jimmy Snuggerud, and STL led the first period 1.52 to 0.76 in expected goals. Dallas then took over the second, 1.37 to 0.23, and still trailed by two after Dalibor Dvorsky snapped one home at 13:05 from a 17 percent chance. Dallas was also 0 for 4 on the power play, with 1.07 expected goals on those chances, and STL went 0 for 4 as well.

The third period settled it. STL was the better team there too, 1.88 to 0.76, and Snuggerud's wrist shot at 17:37 made it 3-0 from a 69 percent look. Fifteen seconds later Pius Suter added another wrist shot at 17:52, with Hofer himself credited with an assist on the play. Dallas won 36 of 58 faceoffs and blocked 19 shots to STL's 12, but none of it produced a goal.
